title: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
syllabus: Morphology and modifications of root, stem, leaf, inflorescence (cymose and racemose), flower, fruit, and seed; Plant tissues (Meristematic and Permanent); Anatomy of root, stem, and leaf; Floral characters and economic importance of Families: Malvaceae, Cruciferae (Brassicaceae), Leguminosae (Fabaceae), Compositae (Asteraceae), and Gramineae (Poaceae).

questions.question: Which of the following families is characterized by having tetradynamous stamens (6 stamens: 4 inner long and 2 outer short) and a bicarpellary, syncarpous ovary with a false septum called replum?
questions.solution: Cruciferae (Brassicaceae, e.g., Brassica/Mustard) is diagnostically distinguished by tetradynamous androecium (4 long inner + 2 short outer stamens), cruciform corolla, and a bicarpellary syncarpous unilocular ovary that becomes bilocular due to the development of a false septum called replum.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of aestivation of petals and their representative examples:

List-I (Aestivation)List-II (Example)
(A) Valvate(I) Cassia and Gulmohur
(B) Twisted(II) Calotropis
(C) Imbricate(III) Pea and Bean
(D) Vexillary (Papilionaceous)(IV) China rose, Lady's finger, Cotton

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Valvate: Calotropis (petals touch without overlapping); Twisted: China rose, Lady's finger, Cotton (one margin overlaps the next); Imbricate: Cassia and Gulmohur (margins overlap non-directionally); Vexillary: Pea and Bean (large standard petal overlaps two lateral wings, which overlap two anterior keels).

questions.question: Monadelphous androecium (stamens united into a single bundle or tube surrounding the style) and reniform/monothecous anthers are characteristic features of which plant family?
questions.solution: Malvaceae (e.g., Hibiscus rosa-sinensis/China rose, Cotton, Okra) is characterized by a staminal tube formed by the fusion of filaments (monadelphous condition), epicalyx, and kidney-shaped (reniform) monothecous anthers.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding root modifications and their functions:

List-I (Root Type)List-II (Plant Example & Function)
(A) Pneumatophores(I) Zea mays (Maize) - Mechanical support from lower nodes
(B) Prop roots(II) Rhizophora - Respiratory gas exchange in halophytes
(C) Stilt roots(III) Ficus benghalensis (Banyan) - Pillar-like aerial support
(D) Tuberous tap root(IV) Daucus carota (Carrot) - Food storage

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Pneumatophores: Rhizophora (respiration in saline swamps); Prop roots: Ficus benghalensis (pillar-like support from branches); Stilt roots: Zea mays / Sugarcane (support from lower stem nodes); Tuberous tap root: Carrot/Radish (food storage).

questions.question: In inflorescences, racemose differs fundamentally from cymose inflorescence because in racemose inflorescence:
options: The main peduncle continues to grow indefinitely and flowers are borne laterally in acropetal succession
The main axis terminates in a flower, limiting growth and flowers open in basipetal order
Centrifugal opening of flowers occurs with peduncle branching
Flowers are always sessile and unisexual
questions.solution: In racemose inflorescence, the main axis (peduncle) does not terminate in a flower and continues indefinite vegetative growth, producing flowers laterally in an acropetal (youngest near apex, oldest at base) succession. In cymose, the main axis terminates in a flower (determinate growth) with basipetal flower development.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of placentation in ovaries:

List-I (Placentation)List-II (Example)
(A) Marginal(I) Dianthus and Primrose
(B) Axile(II) Sunflower and Marigold
(C) Parietal(III) Pea
(D) Free central(IV) Mustard and Argemone
(E) Basal(V) Tomato, Lemon, and China rose

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Marginal: Pea (ridge along ventral suture); Axile: Tomato, Lemon, China rose (multilocular with central axis); Parietal: Mustard, Argemone (inner ovary wall); Free central: Dianthus, Primrose (central axis without septa); Basal: Sunflower, Marigold (base of ovary with single ovule).

questions.question: Ray florets and disc florets organized inside a head (capitulum) inflorescence surrounded by an involucre of bracts are diagnostic features of family:
questions.solution: Compositae (Asteraceae, e.g., Helianthus annuus/Sunflower, Marigold) bears a racemose head or capitulum inflorescence consisting of central tubular bisexual disc florets and peripheral zygomorphic, ligulate ray florets with a pappus calyx and basal placentation.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the floral characteristics of Fabaceae (Papilionoideae):
Statement I: The corolla shows vexillary aestivation with 1 large standard (vexillum), 2 lateral wings (alae), and 2 fused anterior keels (carina).
Statement II: Androecium is diadelphous with $(9) + 1$ stamen arrangement, and the gynoecium is monocarpellary, unilocular with marginal placentation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Fabaceae is identified by zygomorphic flowers with papilionaceous/vexillary corolla (1 standard + 2 wings + 2 keels), diadelphous stamens $[(9) + 1]$, and a superior monocarpellary ovary with marginal placentation yielding a legume fruit.

questions.question: In a caryopsis (grain) fruit of family Gramineae (Poaceae, e.g., Maize, Wheat), the shield-shaped single large cotyledon is known as:
questions.solution: In monocotyledonous grass seeds (Family Gramineae/Poaceae), the single, large, shield-shaped cotyledon situated toward the lateral side of the embryonal axis is called the scutellum. Coleoptile and coleorhiza are protective sheaths enclosing the plumule and radicle respectively.

questions.question: Casparian strips are waterproof suberized bands present in the radial and tangential walls of which anatomical layer of the root?
questions.solution: The innermost layer of the root cortex is the endodermis, comprising single-layered barrel-shaped cells lacking intercellular spaces. Their tangential and radial walls have localized deposition of water-impermeable, waxy suberin called Casparian strips, enforcing symplastic water flow.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding simple plant tissues and their structural/functional characteristics:

List-I (Tissue)List-II (Characteristic Feature)
(A) Parenchyma(I) Highly thickened, lignified dead cells with narrow lumina and pits
(B) Collenchyma(II) Living cells with uneven pectin, cellulose, and hemicellulose corner wall thickenings
(C) Sclerenchyma(III) Thin-walled isodiametric living cells with active storage, photosynthesis, and secretion

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Parenchyma: Living, thin-walled cellulosic cells responsible for photosynthesis, storage, and secretion; Collenchyma: Living cells with localized corner thickenings of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin providing tensile mechanical support to growing stems/petioles; Sclerenchyma: Dead, highly lignified thick-walled cells providing mechanical rigidity.

questions.question: Bulliform or 'motor' cells are large, empty, colorless, bubble-shaped adaxial epidermal cells found on the leaves of:
questions.solution: In monocot grass leaves (Family Gramineae/Poaceae), certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify into large, empty, colorless, highly turgid bulliform cells. When flaccid during water stress, they cause the leaf to roll inward to minimize transpiration loss.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the anatomical comparison between Dicot Stem and Monocot Stem:

List-I (Stem Type)List-II (Anatomical Arrangement)
(A) Dicotyledonous stem(I) Scattered vascular bundles, closed, surrounded by sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, no pith
(B) Monocotyledonous stem(II) Ring arrangement of vascular bundles, conjoint, collateral, open with intrafascicular cambium

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Dicot stem: Vascular bundles arranged in a distinct concentric ring, conjoint, collateral, and open (containing intrafascicular cambium) with distinct central parenchymatous pith. Monocot stem: Numerous vascular bundles scattered throughout ground tissue, closed (no cambium), surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.

questions.question: A drupe fruit (such as Mango and Coconut) develops from a:
options: Monocarpellary, superior ovary and is one-seeded
Bicarpellary, inferior ovary and is multi-seeded
Polycarpellary, syncarpous superior ovary with axile placentation
Monocarpellary, inferior ovary with parietal placentation
questions.solution: In mango (Mangifera indica) and coconut (Cocos nucifera), the fruit is a drupe. It develops from a monocarpellary, superior ovary and is unilocular and single-seeded. In mango, the mesocarp is fleshy and edible; in coconut, the mesocarp is fibrous.

questions.question: In a dorsiventral (dicotyledonous) leaf, the mesophyll tissue situated between upper and lower epidermis is differentiated into:
options: Adaxially placed columnar palisade parenchyma and abaxially placed loose spongy parenchyma
Collenchymatous palisade and parenchymatous bulliform tissue
questions.solution: In a dicot dorsiventral leaf, the mesophyll consists of two distinct regions: (1) Palisade parenchyma placed adaxially (upper side), made of vertically elongated, compact columnar cells, and (2) Spongy parenchyma placed abaxially (lower side), composed of oval/round loosely arranged cells with large air cavities.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the specialized stem modifications and their examples:

List-I (Stem Modification)List-II (Plant Example)
(A) Phylloclade (Photosynthetic fleshy green stem)(I) Eichhornia and Pistia
(B) Stem tendril(II) Opuntia (flattened) / Euphorbia (cylindrical)
(C) Stem thorn (Defensive woody organ)(III) Gourds (Cucumber, Pumpkin) and Grapevine
(D) Offset (Aquatic lateral branch)(IV) Bougainvillea and Citrus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Phylloclade: Opuntia/Euphorbia (stems become green, succulent, and photosynthetic); Stem tendrils: Cucumber, Pumpkin, Grapevine (modified axillary buds for climbing); Stem thorns: Citrus, Bougainvillea (hard, woody, pointed axillary protective organs); Offsets: Pistia, Eichhornia (short lateral runners with rosettes of leaves).

questions.question: Floral formula $\oplus \; \text{K}_{(5)} \; \text{C}_{1+2+(2)} \; \text{A}_{(9)+1} \; \underline{\text{G}}_1$ is mathematically and taxonomically diagnostic of the family:
questions.solution: The floral formula of Fabaceae (Papilionoideae) is: $\% \; \text{K}_{(5)} \; \text{C}_{1+2+(2)} \; \text{A}_{(9)+1} \; \underline{\text{G}}_1$ (Zygomorphic, gamosepalous calyx of 5, polypetalous papilionaceous corolla, diadelphous 10 stamens, monocarpellary superior ovary).

questions.question: Which of the following elements of complex permanent tissue xylem lacks living protoplasm and functions as dead, lignified, elongated water-conducting tubes?
questions.solution: Tracheids, Vessels, and Xylem fibres are dead, highly lignified elements lacking protoplasm at maturity that conduct water and mineral sap under negative tension. Xylem parenchyma is the only living component in xylem.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the anatomical zones of a developing root tip:

List-I (Zone of Root)List-II (Functional Feature)
(A) Root Cap(I) Region of rapid cell division, dense protoplasm, and small thin-walled cells
(B) Region of Meristematic Activity(II) Thimble-like parenchymatous protective structure at root apex
(C) Region of Elongation(III) Differentiated mature cells bearing unicellular epidermal root hairs for water absorption
(D) Region of Maturation(IV) Rapid enlargement and lengthening of cells responsible for root growth in length

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Root cap: Protective thimble-like structure covering root apex; Meristematic zone: Actively dividing small, thin-walled cells with dense cytoplasm; Elongation zone: Cells undergo rapid elongation responsible for root growth; Maturation zone: Cells differentiate and form epidermal root hairs for absorption.

questions.question: Phyllode (petiole modified into a flat, green, photosynthetic leaf-like structure) is found in:
questions.solution: In Australian Acacia, the normal compound lamina falls off early, and the petiole expands into a green, sickle-shaped photosynthetic structure called a phyllode.

questions.question: A spikelet inflorescence enclosed by glumes, palea, and lemma with versatile anthers and feathery stigma is characteristic of family:
questions.solution: Gramineae (Poaceae, grass family including Rice, Wheat, Sugarcane) bears spikelet inflorescences surrounded by sterile glumes, lemmas, palea, lodicules (reduced perianth), versatile stamens, and feathery bifid stigmas adapted for wind pollination (anemophily).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding leaf phyllotaxy (pattern of arrangement of leaves on stem):

List-I (Phyllotaxy)List-II (Plant Example)
(A) Alternate(I) Calotropis and Guava
(B) Opposite(II) Alstonia
(C) Whorled(III) China rose, Mustard, and Sunflower

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Alternate phyllotaxy (single leaf at each node): China rose, Mustard, Sunflower; Opposite phyllotaxy (pair of leaves arise at each node opposite each other): Calotropis, Guava; Whorled phyllotaxy (more than two leaves arise at a node forming a circle): Alstonia.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about phloem tissue in angiosperms is INCORRECT?
options: Mature sieve tube elements lack a nucleus but remain alive and metabolically controlled by the nucleus of companion cells.
Companion cells are specialized parenchymatous cells connected to sieve tubes by pit fields.
Phloem parenchyma is present in all monocotyledons without exception.
Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are sclerenchymatous dead cells that provide mechanical strength.
questions.solution: Phloem parenchyma is absent in most monocotyledons. Sieve tube elements are enucleate at maturity but functional due to companion cells. Phloem fibres are the only dead elements in angiosperm phloem.

questions.question: Epigynous flowers with an inferior ovary enclosed by the fused thalamus/receptacle are found in:
options: Cucumber, Guava, and ray florets of Sunflower
questions.solution: In epigynous flowers, the margin of thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it; the other parts arise above the ovary, making the ovary inferior (e.g., Guava, Cucumber, ray florets of Sunflower). Mustard/China rose are hypogynous; Plum/Rose/Peach are perigynous.

questions.question: Radial vascular bundles, where xylem and phloem strands occur alternately on different radii separated by conjunctive tissue, are found in:
questions.solution: In roots (both dicot and monocot), the primary vascular bundles are arranged radially (xylem and phloem lie on separate radii alternating with parenchymatous conjunctive tissue). In stems and leaves, vascular bundles are conjoint.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the floral formulas and botanical families:

List-I (Family)List-II (Characteristic Floral Formula)
(A) Cruciferae(I) $\oplus \; \text{K}_{(5)} \; \text{C}_{5} \; \text{A}_{(\infty)} \; \underline{\text{G}}_{(5-\infty)}$
(B) Malvaceae(II) $\oplus \; \text{K}_{2+2} \; \text{C}_{4} \; \text{A}_{2+4} \; \underline{\text{G}}_{(2)}$
(C) Compositae (Ray floret)(III) $\% \; \text{K}_{\text{pappus}} \; \text{C}_{(5)} \; \text{A}_{0} \; \overline{\text{G}}_{(2)}$
(D) Gramineae(IV) $\% \; \text{P}_{2(\text{lodicules})} \; \text{A}_{3} \; \underline{\text{G}}_{1}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Cruciferae: $\oplus \; \text{K}_{2+2} \; \text{C}_{4} \; \text{A}_{2+4} \; \underline{\text{G}}_{(2)}$; Malvaceae: $\oplus \; \text{K}_{(5)} \; \text{C}_{5} \; \text{A}_{(\infty)} \; \underline{\text{G}}_{(5-\infty)}$; Compositae (ray floret): $\% \; \text{K}_{\text{pappus}} \; \text{C}_{(5)} \; \text{A}_{0} \; \overline{\text{G}}_{(2)}$; Gramineae: $\% \; \text{P}_{2(\text{lodicules})} \; \text{A}_{3} \; \underline{\text{G}}_{1}$.

questions.question: Syngenesious androecium (anthers fused into a tube around the style while filaments remain free) and epipetalous stamens are found in family:
questions.solution: In family Compositae (Asteraceae), disc florets have syngenesious (synantherous) androecium where all 5 anthers are fused along their margins into a cylinder while filaments remain free and epipetalous.

questions.question: The stomatal apparatus consists of stomatal aperture guarded by two kidney-shaped guard cells, which in grasses are:
questions.solution: In dicots, guard cells are bean- or kidney-shaped with thick inner walls. In grasses (Family Gramineae/Poaceae), the guard cells are distinctly dumbbell-shaped.

questions.question: In a dicotyledonous root, the vascular bundles are characterized as:
options: Diarch to hexarch with exarch xylem
questions.solution: Dicot roots possess 2 to 4 (rarely up to 6, i.e., diarch to hexarch) radial xylem and phloem patches with exarch protoxylem (protoxylem directed toward periphery, metaxylem toward centre). Monocot roots have polyarch (>6) xylem bundles.

questions.question: Which of the following plants belongs to the family Malvaceae and provides commercial natural textile fibre obtained from epidermal seed hairs?
questions.solution: Gossypium (Cotton) belongs to family Malvaceae; its raw economic fibres are unicellular cellulose-rich epidermal seed coat hairs. (Sunnhemp belongs to Fabaceae; Jute to Tiliaceae).

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the anatomy of a monocotyledonous root:
Statement I: It has polyarch xylem bundles (usually more than six) and a large, well-developed central parenchymatous pith.
Statement II: It does not undergo any secondary growth due to absence of vascular and cork cambium.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Monocot roots have more than 6 (polyarch) xylem bundles, a prominent large parenchymatous pith, and lack cambium, undergoing no secondary growth.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the plant families and their economic food/oil crops:

List-I (Family)List-II (Economic Crop Example)
(A) Cruciferae(I) Abelmoschus esculentus (Bhindi/Lady's finger)
(B) Malvaceae(II) Brassica campestris (Mustard/Rapeseed)
(C) Fabaceae(III) Helianthus annuus (Sunflower) and Carthamus (Safflower)
(D) Compositae(IV) Cicer arietinum (Gram) and Glycine max (Soybean)
(E) Gramineae(V) Triticum aestivum (Wheat) and Oryza sativa (Paddy)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Cruciferae: Mustard (Brassica); Malvaceae: Lady's finger (Abelmoschus); Fabaceae: Gram (Cicer) and Soybean (Glycine); Compositae: Sunflower (Helianthus); Gramineae: Wheat (Triticum) and Rice (Oryza).

questions.question: In a dicotyledonous stem undergoing secondary growth, the interfascicular cambium originates from the dedifferentiation of:
questions.solution: During secondary growth in dicot stems, the parenchymatous cells of the medullary rays adjoining the intrafascicular cambium become meristematic (dedifferentiation) and form the interfascicular cambium, completing a continuous cambial ring.

questions.question: In a maize (monocot) stem, the vascular bundles are described as:
options: Conjoint, collateral, closed, and endarch with Y-shaped xylem vessels and a lysigenous water cavity
questions.solution: In monocot stems (e.g., Maize), each vascular bundle is conjoint, collateral, closed (without cambium), surrounded by a sclerenchymatous sheath, with endarch protoxylem forming a characteristic lysigenous protoxylem water cavity (lacuna) and Y-shaped metaxylem vessels.

questions.question: A typical papilionaceous flower has 10 stamens in two bundles ($9$ united into a gutter-like tube and $1$ posterior stamen free). This condition is known as:
questions.solution: When stamens are grouped into two separate bundles, the condition is termed diadelphous (e.g., $(9) + 1$ arrangement in Fabaceae/Pea).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the fruit types and their botanical classification:

List-I (Fruit Type)List-II (Defining Feature & Family)
(A) Siliqua(I) Dehiscent dry fruit from monocarpellary ovary opening along both sutures (Fabaceae)
(B) Legume (Pod)(II) Dry dehiscent fruit from bicarpellary ovary opening from base to apex by replum (Cruciferae)
(C) Cypsela(III) Single-seeded dry indehiscent fruit with pericarp completely fused with seed coat (Gramineae)
(D) Caryopsis(IV) Dry single-seeded indehiscent fruit from inferior bicarpellary ovary with pappus (Compositae)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Siliqua: Cruciferae (2 valves opening from below leaving replum); Legume: Fabaceae (opens along ventral and dorsal sutures); Cypsela: Compositae (inferior unilocular single-seeded fruit with pappus); Caryopsis: Gramineae (pericarp and testa fused).

questions.question: The epicalyx (a whorl of bracteoles located outside the calyx) is a distinctive diagnostic field character of family:
questions.solution: An epicalyx (involucre of bracteoles occurring just beneath the calyx whorl) is a prominent characteristic of Family Malvaceae (e.g., Hibiscus, Cotton).

questions.question: Which of the following tissues is dead at maturity and consists of highly thickened lignified cells with narrow lumens, commonly found in fruit pulp of Guava, Pear, and Sapota?
questions.solution: Sclereids (gritty stone cells) are spherical, oval, or cylindrical, highly thickened, dead sclerenchymatous cells with narrow cavities that provide the gritty texture in the fruit pulp of pear, guava, and sapota, and in the seed coats of legumes.

questions.question: Collenchyma differs from parenchyma in possessing:
options: Localized wall thickenings of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin at cell corners
Lignified secondary walls with bordered pits
Dead protoplasm with large air spaces
questions.solution: Collenchyma consists of living cells with localized corner thickenings composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin, providing flexible mechanical support to young dicot stems and petiole margins.

questions.question: In an isobilateral (monocotyledonous) leaf, the stomata are:
options: Present roughly equally on both the adaxial and abaxial epidermis (amphistomatic)
Present strictly on the lower abaxial surface only (hypostomatic)
Present only on the upper adaxial surface (epistomatic)
questions.solution: In monocot isobilateral leaves, stomata are distributed almost equally on both upper (adaxial) and lower (abaxial) epidermes (amphistomatic condition), and the mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy layers.

questions.question: Which of the following plants belongs to family Fabaceae and serves as an important medicinal plant containing glycyrrhizin used as a demulcent and expectorant?
questions.solution: Glycyrrhiza glabra (Muliathi/Liquorice) belongs to family Fabaceae and is an important medicinal plant. (Atropa belongs to Solanaceae; Aloe and Colchicum to Liliaceae).

questions.question: In roots, the pericycle cells give rise to:
options: Lateral root branches and parts of vascular cambium
questions.solution: In roots, the pericycle is thick-walled and parenchymatous or sclerenchymatous; initiation of lateral roots and part of the vascular cambium during secondary growth takes place in these pericyclic cells (endogenous origin of lateral roots).

questions.question: The calyx modified into a persistent hairy or bristly structure called 'pappus' that aids in wind parachute dispersal of cypsela fruits is found in:
questions.solution: In Compositae (Asteraceae, e.g., Sunflower, Dandelion), the calyx is modified into a persistent hairy ring called pappus, which functions as a parachute mechanism for anemochorous fruit dispersal.

questions.question: Phellogen (cork cambium), phellem (cork), and phelloderm (secondary cortex) are collectively designated as:
questions.solution: Phellogen (cork cambium) cuts off phellem (cork with suberized walls) toward the outside and phelloderm (secondary parenchymatous cortex) toward the inside. These three layers together constitute the periderm.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Heartwood (duramen) consists of dead, lignified elements loaded with tannins, resins, and oils, and does not conduct water.
Statement II: Sapwood (alburnum) is the peripheral, lighter-colored region of secondary xylem that actively conducts water and mineral sap.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. In older dicot trees, the central non-functional heartwood provides mechanical support and resists microbial attack due to deposits of tannins/resins/essential oils, while the peripheral sapwood actively conducts water from roots to leaves.
